Consuelo OS ships with skill templates that you can enable or remove after installation.

## Add a skill

Run the picker:

```bash
consuelo add skill
```

The picker shows only skill templates that are not currently selected.

To add one or more skills directly:

```bash
consuelo add skill branch
consuelo add skill branch browser debugger
```

Unknown bundled skill names fail instead of creating a silent configuration entry.

## Remove a skill

Run the installed-skill picker:

```bash
consuelo remove skill
```

Or remove by name:

```bash
consuelo remove skill branch
```

A clean managed skill is removed from the visible `~/Consuelo/Skills/<name>/` tree. If you modified the managed copy locally, Consuelo removes it from the selected set but preserves those files for explicit review.

## What changes

Skill selection updates one canonical intent and then reconciles the derived surfaces:

```text
<CONSUELO_HOME>/config.json
  selectedSkills              # durable desired set

<CONSUELO_HOME>/components/installed-skills.json
                              # active managed index

~/Consuelo/Skills/<name>/     # visible selected skill copy
~/Consuelo/Skills/skills.json # full bundled catalog
```

On the next normal agent bootstrap, steering reads the active installed index and advertises selected skills that are not disabled by the manifest overlay.

## Verify

After adding a skill, check that:

1. its name is present in `config.json.selectedSkills`;
2. it appears in `components/installed-skills.json`;
3. `~/Consuelo/Skills/<name>/SKILL.md` exists;
4. a fresh agent bootstrap lists it in Installed skills.

See the individual pages in [Skill Templates](/build/skills/bundled/) for each skill's purpose and boundary.

## Custom skill note

The current `add skill` command selects skill templates. Existing custom skills from the legacy hidden `<CONSUELO_HOME>/skills/` tree are preserved for migration; the CLI does not treat an arbitrary new folder name as a bundled install.
